name: Advanced Filesystem: Antivirus (ClamAV)
description: Scans uploaded files for malware with ClamAV (clamd INSTREAM over TCP/Unix socket, or the clamdscan/clamscan CLI). Blocks, warns or quarantines infected uploads, bulk-scans existing files (batch + Drush), and keeps a detection log. Sub-module of Advanced Filesystem.

suggests.drush/drush: ^12 — enables the adfs:av:ping and adfs:av:scan CLI commands.

project_description: The Antivirus sub-module of Advanced Filesystem integrates ClamAV to scan uploaded files for malware. The ClamAvScanner service supports four connection modes: streaming file bytes to the clamd daemon via the INSTREAM command over a TCP socket or a Unix domain socket (preferred — the daemon needs no filesystem access), or shelling out to the clamdscan / clamscan binaries. CLI invocation goes through proc_open with every argument passed through escapeshellarg. An AntivirusFileValidator subscriber to the core FileValidationEvent scans new uploads and, per the on_infection setting, blocks (adds a validation violation and quarantines the file), warns, or just logs; a fail_closed toggle controls whether an unscannable file is rejected. Infected detections are written to the adfs_antivirus_log table, optionally dispatched to the Webhooks sub-module, and recorded in the parent module's audit log. Existing files can be bulk-scanned through a Batch form or the adfs:av:scan Drush command (adfs:av:ping checks connectivity), and a detection-log controller plus a settings form (connection mode, host/port/socket, size cap, action, quarantine directory, retention) round it out. All routes and the log are gated by the restricted 'administer advanced_filesystem_antivirus' permission.
